issues.failure_explanation: For the Nitsche form in eq:forms, continuity A_h(v,w) <= C |||v||| |||w||| holds for every beta > 0 (each term is dominated by the corresponding energy-norm factor), whereas coercivity on V_h holds only for beta sufficiently large: the indefinite term -2(nabla_{n_delta} v, v) on the boundary must be absorbed into beta h^{-1}||v||^2_{boundary} via trace/inverse inequalities (controlled through the stabilization assumption). As written, coercivity is asserted unconditionally and continuity only 'for beta>0 sufficiently large' — the qualifier sits on the wrong property, so the coercivity claim is false as stated for small beta (cf. the large fixed choice beta=25p^2 used in the experiments).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Move the qualifier 'for beta>0 sufficiently large' from the continuity statement to the coercivity statement; continuity holds for all beta > 0. A one-clause standard correction after which every downstream argument applies unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated properties of A_h are incorrect as written; the Lax--Milgram well-posedness, the stability estimate eq:stability, the discrete dual stability eq:dual-stab, and all subsequent error analyses invoke coercivity and therefore implicitly rely on the corrected statement.
issues.title: Large-penalty condition attached to continuity instead of coercivity
issues.why_classification: Forced, local relocation of the penalty condition; no claim, rate, or guarantee is lost and no new argument is required.

For v in H^s(Omega) with 1 <= s <= 3/2, nabla v^e in H^{s-1} has no such trace, so the left-hand side of eq:interpol-energy is not defined on part of the stated range 1 <= s <= p+1; the bound is meaningful only for s > 3/2.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the stated range to 3/2 < s <= p+1 (or s >= 2); every use in the paper complies.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed supporting estimate is overstated. It is applied in the paper only with s >= 2 (to u^e in H^{p+1}, p >= 1, and to the H^2 dual solution in the L^2 proof), so no proof step is actually affected.
issues.title: Energy-norm interpolation estimate stated on a range where its left side is undefined (s <= 3/2)
issues.why_classification: Pure parameter-range correction of a supporting estimate; all applications lie inside the valid range, so nothing downstream changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:strip is stated under the hypothesis Omega subset Omega_delta, but Theorem thm:energy-error assumes only the boundary closeness conditions, which allow Omega not subset Omega_delta (e.g., interlaced boundaries with both mismatch sets nonempty). The theorem applies the lemma to ||v||_{Omega_delta setminus Omega} (eq:strip-estimate-energy) without verifying the inclusion, and the same estimate is reused in thm:h1-error (Term II, via eq:prelim-energy-error) and thm:l2-error (Term II, eq:l2-termII-dual-strip). The lemma's proof never uses the inclusion Omega subset Omega_delta — it only integrates over the mismatch set inside the tubular neighborhood U_delta of the boundary — so the applications remain valid once the lemma is restated; as written, statement and use are misaligned.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the hypothesis Omega subset Omega_delta from Lemma lem:strip (keeping only the tube inclusion of the mismatch set, which follows from the standing geometric assumptions); the given proof then literally covers every application.
issues.overall_effect: Formally, the strip estimate entering the residual bounds of all three error theorems rests on a lemma cited outside its stated scope. The conclusions themselves remain correct because the lemma's proof already covers the general mismatch region.
issues.title: Domain mismatch lemma invoked outside its stated hypothesis Omega subset Omega_delta
issues.why_classification: The needed estimate is already proved; only the lemma's stated scope must be widened to match its use — a local restatement with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The second inequality of eq:u-star-hp1-bound is false at the order s = p+1 at which it is used. Because u^e o q_delta is constant along normals to the boundary, its H^{p+1}-norm on the tube is equivalent to the H^{p+1}-norm of the trace u^e|_{boundary} (flat case: u o q_delta(x',x_d) = g(x') has tube norm (2c)^{1/2} ||g||_{H^{p+1}}), while the trace of a general u^e in H^{p+1}(U) lies only in H^{p+1/2} of the boundary; by surjectivity of the trace map there exist u^e in H^{p+1}(U) whose trace is not in H^{p+1} of the boundary, i.e., u^e o q_delta not in H^{p+1}(U) at all. A half derivative is therefore lost. The steps I_1 (eq:i-first-term), I_{2,1} (eq:grad-pi-u-star), I_{2,2}, and I_{2,3} each rely on eq:u-star-hp1-bound with s = p+1 to convert h^p ||u^e_*||_{H^{p+1}} into h^p ||u||_{H^{p+1}(Omega)}, and are thus unsupported. With the valid bound ||u^e_*||_{H^{p+1/2}} <= C ||u^e||_{H^{p+1}} the same computations yield only h^{p-1/2} ||u||_{H^{p+1}}, so under the stated assumptions (u in H^{p+1}(Omega), u^e in W^2_infty cap H^{2+eps} near the boundary) the proof establishes a half-order lower rate than the h^p claimed in Theorem thm:h1-error. (For p = 1 the assumed W^2_infty regularity directly gives u^e_* in H^2, so the p = 1 statement survives.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the boundary regularity assumption by half a derivative — assume u^e in H^{p+3/2} on a neighborhood of the approximate boundary (equivalently u^e restricted to the approximate boundary in H^{p+1} of it) and use the corresponding stronger norm on the right-hand side; then eq:u-star-hp1-bound holds at s = p+1 and every step of the proof goes through with the stated rates h^p + delta + delta_n preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central refined estimate thm:h1-error — and its restatements in the abstract, the introduction (eq:intro-h1-norm-error), the 'Summary of Geometric Requirements' in Section 5, and the conclusions — is not proved as stated: for p >= 2 the argument supports only h^{p-1/2} + delta_n + delta under H^{p+1} data. The energy and L^2 theorems do not use u^e_* and are unaffected.
issues.title: Sobolev bound for the normal extension u^e_* loses half a derivative; optimal H^1 rate unproved under stated regularity
issues.why_classification: The defect genuinely invalidates the optimal-rate proof for p >= 2 (without repair the argument loses half an order), but a contained strengthening of the regularity hypothesis restores the full statement with identical rates, structure, and qualitative conclusions — a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable theorem, requiring no new proof architecture; hence more than minor but not serious.
